skill.name: alchemist
skill.description: Build, change, test and publish Olbrain AI agents (chat agents, automatic jobs, teams of agents and research agents) with Alchemist, Olbrain's agent builder. Use when the user wants to create or edit an Olbrain agent, asks what Alchemist can do or whether it can do something, get suggestions for which agents their business needs and their requirements documents, check on a build, answer an Alchemist approval card, see an agent as a diagram, put a live agent on their website or call it from their app's code, raise or follow up their Olbrain support tickets, or set up their Olbrain organisation.
skill.summary: Build, test, and manage chat agents, automated jobs, agent teams, and research agents in Olbrain.
skill.author: olbrain

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown or routine account operations, not shell execution or host reconnaissance. The documented server integration uses an organisation-wide API key, and a job test can upload a user-selected file to Olbrain. The review also found weak approval defaults, unclear data-sharing limits, and a staff upload that passes a tool-returned URL to the shell.

remediation.issue: Automatic client mode is treated as delegation to answer approval cards.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit, scoped delegation for automatic answers and fresh confirmation for any charge, data sharing, permission change, or production change.

remediation.issue: The staff upload inserts a URL from a tool result into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured HTTPS client without shell interpolation. Validate the exact destination, disallow redirects, and keep signed URLs out of logs.

remediation.issue: The generated server integration uses a key that can call any agent in the organisation.
remediation.suggestion: Use agent-scoped credentials where available. Keep keys in a server-side secret store and enforce authentication and usage limits.

remediation.issue: Build inputs can draw on repository files, documents, websites, and earlier messages without a clear sharing boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Preview what will be sent to Olbrain, include only necessary details, redact sensitive information, and ask before sending private material.

remediation.issue: Remote workflow text can be treated as instructions without an explicit bound to the current user request.
remediation.suggestion: Validate workflow state against a fixed schema and local action policy. Verify the source and scope of queued requests before acting on them.

remediation.issue: The staff workflow treats a screen request as permission to release its first version.
remediation.suggestion: Require separate confirmation before pushing, merging, or publishing. Show the target organisation, repository, revision, audience, and agent bindings.

remediation.issue: A test can send a user-selected file to Olbrain.
remediation.suggestion: Show the file, destination agent, and retention terms before upload. Recommend synthetic test data and keep the option to skip.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Mode Substitutes for User Delegation
semantic_findings.description: The skill defaults to answering cards automatically when client approvals are disabled. This can approve a website connection without a specific user decision.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default is explicit, and the website card documents assistant-provided origins. Certain publishing and destructive actions still require separate confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Build Context Has No Explicit Sharing Boundary
semantic_findings.description: The skill forwards requests verbatim and uses repository files, documents, websites, and earlier messages to draft build inputs. Private information may reach Olbrain.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly forwards user messages and draws on local context. It protects listed secrets but does not require review of other sensitive material.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Workflow State Can Direct Assistant Actions
semantic_findings.description: The assistant follows instructions returned in build state and treats queued messages as user instructions. It has no documented local check against the current request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill distinguishes untrusted output but grants these fields authority. The service's validation and account binding are not visible in the reviewed files.

semantic_findings.title: Staff Upload Passes a Tool-Returned URL to the Shell
semantic_findings.description: The staff workflow inserts a tool-returned URL directly into a shell command. Quoting and a storage URL prefix check do not prevent shell interpretation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions prescribe direct insertion and only validate the URL prefix and content type. They do not require shell-safe argument handling.

semantic_findings.description: The staff workflow treats a screen request as permission to push changes, merge the review branch, and publish the first version to the active organisation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly includes first publication in the build and only requires an explicit request for later versions. It still requires pull request review.

content.value_statement: Turning a business process into an agent requires clear requirements, tests, and release decisions. Alchemist uses Olbrain tools to build agents and track those steps.
actual_capabilities: Build or revise Olbrain chat agents, automated jobs, agent teams, and research agents.
Find existing builds, track progress, and report pending approval cards.
Draft requirements and tests, then report how Alchemist graded the tests it ran.
Request a read-only diagram of an agent draft or published version.
Get connection steps for a live agent on a website or in a server application.
Open or update Olbrain support tickets when requested.
limitations: Requires an Olbrain account, an active organisation, and an Alchemist connection in the client.
Available actions depend on the connected tools, account role, service limits, and agent status.
Live runs consume organisation credits, and actions such as publishing an agent require the user's approval.
Screen development tools are available only to verified Olbrain staff.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Capability
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether Alchemist supports an agent that answers product questions from a help centre. Do not start a build.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm platform support before defining a build.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Chat Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an agent that answers shipping questions and refers refund requests to staff. Ask before submitting private data or approving any card.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: create a draft with a clear handoff rule.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Tests for an Automated Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the weekly reporting build. Propose tests for missing inputs and duplicate records using synthetic data. Ask before running tests or changing the schedule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review failure cases before a billed test.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Server Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Find my live support agent and show its server integration options. Explain key scope, user authentication, rate limits, and session ownership. Do not edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review an integration before implementation.

output_examples.input: Show me the status of the returns assistant build.
output_examples.output: The returns assistant is still a draft. Alchemist is waiting for your decision on how the agent should handle exceptions to the return policy.

output_examples.input: Show me how to connect my live help centre agent without changing my site.
output: The website widget needs the site's allowed origin.
A custom interface needs a server route that keeps the Olbrain key out of browser code.
No files were changed and no test messages were sent.

best_practices: Confirm the active organisation and agent before editing a build or opening a connection.
Review information before sending it to Olbrain and use synthetic data for tests.
Keep keys on the server and require explicit approval for publishing, sharing, or billed runs.
anti_patterns: Do not paste access keys or signing secrets into chat or add them to browser code.
Do not submit the same build request again while it is still running.
Do not rely on automatic client mode as permission to answer approval cards.

faq.question: What types of agents can I build?
faq.answer: Olbrain Alchemist supports chat agents, automated jobs, agent teams, and research agents.

faq.question: What do I need to connect?
faq.answer: You need an Olbrain account and the Alchemist connection in your client. Verify the active organisation before starting a build.

faq.question: Does the skill publish agents without my approval?
faq.answer: Publishing agents requires your approval. Set an explicit card policy because automatic mode may answer other cards when you have not specified one.

faq.question: Do test runs use credits?
faq.answer: Live tests and job runs can consume organisation credits. Ask for a test plan first when you do not want to run anything.

faq.question: Can I connect a live agent to a website?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the website widget or a custom interface backed by a server that keeps the Olbrain key private.

faq.question: Can I publish an Olbrain Screen?
faq.answer: The screen tools are limited to verified Olbrain staff. Connecting screen agents also requires an appropriate role in the active organisation.
